To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
In Sri Lanka, a country with a high burden of antibiotic resistance, we conducted a pseudo-patient survey of 242 community pharmacies.

1) illegal and inappropriate dispensing practices of antibiotics are evident in Sri Lanka; 2) these practices are likely to contribute to the burden of antimicrobial resistance; 3) the presence of a pharmacist reduced illegal dispensing of antibiotics but not inappropriate dispensing; and 4) there is a need to develop and implement strategies to improve the appropriate antibiotic dispensing practice among community pharmacies.
